findings.title: Unsubscribe crashes when no TopicUser row exists
findings.body: TopicsController#unsubscribe loads the user's TopicUser with find_by and immediately reads tu.notification_level. If the recipient has never had a topic_users row (or it was deleted), tu is nil and the action raises NoMethodError instead of unsubscribing. The email link is therefore a 500 for that user, and no muted/regular level is stored. Create the row (TopicUser.change) or no-op safely when it is missing.

findings.title: Level change skips TopicUser.change and does not actually stop watching
findings.body: The action assigns notification_level and calls save! instead of TopicUser.change. That skips notifications_reason_id and notifications_changed_at. auto_track and update_last_read only keep a user-chosen level when notifications_reason_id is set; with it left nil, the next visit or auto-track promotes the user back to tracking, so the unsubscribe does not stick. Separately, watching/tracking (level > regular) is only lowered to regular, not muted, while regular is muted. Watching users still receive reply, mention, and quote mail, which contradicts the new email copy that this link stops notifications for the topic. A second GET then takes the else branch and mutes them, so refresh or a double click changes the level again.

findings.title: Topic unsubscribe is an unauthenticated-token GET that mutates state
findings.body: t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe and t/:topic_id/unsubscribe are GET routes with no per-user unsubscribe key, and TopicsController#unsubscribe writes notification_level as a side effect. Rails CSRF protection does not cover GET, so any site can mute or downgrade a logged-in victim for a known topic id with an img or prefetch of that URL. Mail-gateway link scanners that follow the link in an already logged-in browser do the same. One-click email unsubscribe needs a POST or a secret, user-specific token, and must not depend on an existing session cookie.

findings.title: No specs for the unsubscribe action
findings.body: The only test change passes unsubscribe_url into MessageBuilder and still only asserts that the preferences URL appears. Nothing covers TopicsController#unsubscribe: missing TopicUser, watching vs regular vs muted outcomes, notifications_reason_id being set, idempotent repeats, or the email string interpolating unsubscribe_url. Those paths are where this feature breaks, so the PR can merge with the action crashing or not sticking.
